procnotices.contact_address: Asokoro Highbrow Dutse Jigawa State
procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

CONSULTANT’S QUALIFICATIONS BASED SELECTION (CQS)

Name of Project

Nigeria For Women Program Scale Up-Project (NFPW-SU)

Loan No/Credit No/ Grand Number

Project ID.:  P179447

Assignment Title

Proposed Engagement of an External Audit Firm to provide external Audit Services to the Jigawa State Nigerian For Women Scale-up program for the 2024 -2025 financial year

Procurement Plan Ref Number

NG-JIGAWA NFWP-SU-538153-CS-CQS /

Country of Delivery

Jigawa State, Nigeria.

The Nigeria for Women Project (NFWP) is a flagship initiative of the Federal Government of Nigeria, supported by the World Bank, aimed at enhancing the livelihoods, social inclusion, and economic empowerment of women nationwide. The project acknowledges that gender equality and women's economic empowerment are critical to achieving sustainable development.

As part of the Scale-Up Phase (NFWP-SU), Jigawa State has received credit financing from the International Development Association (IDA) to support project implementation across the state. A portion of this credit will be utilised to engage the services of an external audit firm to provide audit services for the 2024–2025 fiscal year.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this REOI.

In view of the above, the Jigawa State (NFWP-SU), Project Coordinating Unit (SPCU), hereby invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the above-stated Services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Seventh Edition- September 2025)

(“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

The best-qualified firm to carry out the Services will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualifications-Based Selection (CQS) method set out in the Regulations and based on the following criterion: Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: (a) core business and years in business, (b) relevant experience, and (c) technical and managerial capability of the firm. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 9 am to 5 pm, Monday to Friday.

Expressions of interest must be submitted in writing to the address below (in person, by mail, by fax, or by e-mail) by Monday, 18th May 2026.

The Project Coordinator (Jigawa State, NFWP)

Attn: Yusuf Yunusa Abba,

Procurement officer,

Jigawa State, State Project Coordination Unit (SPCU)

Nigerian For Women Scale-Up Program (NFWP-SU)

Email: Jigawa.nigeria4women@gmail.com

No 1 Asokoro G.R.A. Quarters, Dutse, Jigawa State.

Attachment: Terms of Reference (TOR)

 

TERMS OF REFERENCE FOR ENGAGEMENT OF EXTERNAL AUDIT

OF WORLD BANK FINANCED PROJECTS.

NIGERIAN FOR WOMEN PROJECT – SCAHLE-UP PROGRAM(NFWP-S-Up)

 

  1. BACKGROUND

The Nigeria for Women Project (NFWP) is a flagship initiative of the Federal Government of Nigeria, supported by the World Bank, aimed at enhancing the livelihoods, social inclusion, and economic empowerment of women across the country. The project acknowledges that gender equality and women's economic empowerment are critical to achieving sustainable development.

 

  1. OBJECTIVE OF THE PROJECT AUDIT

 

The objective of the audit of the Project. The Nigeria for Women Project (NFWP-S-Up) is to enable the auditor to express a professional opinion(s) on the financial position of the project at the end of each fiscal year, and on funds received and expenditures incurred for the relevant accounting period.

 

The project books of accounts provide the basis for preparation of the PFSs by the project implementing agency and are established to reflect the financial transactions in respect of the project. The implementing agency maintains adequate internal controls and supporting documentation for transactions.

    

  1. PREPARATION OF ANNUAL FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

 

The responsibility for the preparation of financial statements, including adequate disclosure, is that of the implementing agency. The agency is also responsible for the selection and application of accounting policies. The agency would prepare the PFSs in accordance with International Standards on Auditing (ISA).

 

The auditor is responsible for forming and expressing opinions on the financial statements. The auditor would carry out the audit of the project in accordance with the International Standards on Auditing (ISA), as promulgated by the International Federation of Accountants (IFAC). As part of the audit process, the auditor may request from the implementing agency written confirmation concerning representations made in connection with the audit

 

     4.   SCOPE OF THE AUDIT

As stated above, the audit of the project will be carried out in accordance with International Standards on Auditing (ISA) promulgated by the International Federation of Accountants (IFAC) and will include such tests and auditing procedures as the auditor will consider necessary under the circumstances. Special attention should be paid by the auditor as to whether the:

 

  1. World Bank financing (and all external financing where the World Bank is not the only financier) has been used in accordance with the conditions of the relevant financing agreement, with due attention to economy and efficiency, and only for the purposes for which the financing was provided.

 

(b)   Counterpart funds have been provided and used in accordance with the relevant financing agreements, with due attention to economy and efficiency, and only for the purposes for which they were provided;

 

(c)   Goods, works, and services financed have been procured in accordance with the relevant financing agreements, including specific provisions of the World Bank Procurement Policies and Procedures[1];;

 

(d)       All necessary supporting documents, records, and accounts have been maintained in respect of all project activities, including expenditures reported using Statements of Expenditure (SOE) or Interim Unaudited Financial Statements (IFS) methods of reporting. The auditor is expected to verify that the respective reports issued during the period were in agreement with the underlying books of account.

 

  1. Designated Accounts (if used) have been maintained in accordance with the provisions of the relevant financing agreements, and funds disbursed out of the Accounts were used only for the purpose intended in the financing agreement;

 

  1. National laws and regulations have been complied with, and the financial and accounting procedures approved for the project (e.g. operational manual, financial procedures manual, etc.) were followed and used;

 

  1. (g) The project's financial performance is satisfactory.

 

  1. Assets procured from project funds exist and there is verifiable ownership by the implementing agency or beneficiaries in line with the financing agreement.

 

  1. Ineligible expenditures included in withdrawal applications are identified and reimbursed to the Designated Accounts. These should be separately noted in the audit report.

 

In complying with International Standards on Auditing, the auditor is expected to pay particular attention to the following matters:

 

  1. Fraud and Corruption: Consider the risks of material misstatements in the financial statements due to fraud as required by ISA 240: The Auditor’s Responsibility to Consider Fraud in an Audit of Financial Statements. The auditor is required to identify and assess these risks (of material misstatement of the financial statements) due to fraud, obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about the assessed risks, and respond appropriately to identified or suspected fraud.

 

  1. Laws and Regulations: In designing and performing audit procedures, evaluating and reporting the results, consider that noncompliance by the implementing agency with laws and regulations may materially affect the financial statements as required by ISA 250: Consideration of Laws and Regulations in an Audit of Financial Statements;

 

  1. Governance: Communicate audit matters of governance interest arising from the audit of financial statements with those charged with governance of an entity as required by International Standards on Auditing 260: Communication of Audit Matters with those Charged with Governance.

 

  1. Risks: To reduce audit risk to an acceptable low level, determine the overall responses to assessed risks at the financial statement level, and design and perform further audit procedures to respond to assessed risks at the assertion level as required by Internal Standard on Auditing 330: The Auditor’s Procedures in Response to Assessed Risks.

 

5.         PROJECT FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (PFSs)

The auditor should verify that the project PFSs have been prepared in accordance with the agreed accounting standards (see paragraph 3 above) and give a true and fair view of the financial position of the project at the relevant date and of resources and expenditures for the financial year ended on that date

 

           

 

The Project Financial Statements (PFSs) should include:

 

            (a)   A statement of funds received, showing funds from the World Bank, project funds from other donors, and counterpart funds separately, and of expenditures incurred;

 

            (b)   A summary of the activity in the Designated Account;

 

            (b)   A Balance Sheet (if deemed necessary);

 

  1. A Summary of the principal accounting policies that have been adopted, and other explanatory notes;
  2. A list of material assets acquired or procured to date with project funds

 

As an Annex to the PFSs, the auditor should prepare a reconciliation of the amounts as “received by the Project from the World Bank”, with those shown as being disbursed by the Bank. 

 

6.         STATEMENT OF EXPENDITURES (SOEs)/UNAUDITED INTERIM FINANCIAL REPORTS (IFRs)

 

In addition to the audit of the PFSs, the auditor is required to verify all SOEs or IFRs used as a basis for the submission of loan withdrawal applications to the World Bank.  The auditor will apply such tests and auditing procedures as are considered necessary under the circumstances.  Annexed to the PFSs should be a schedule listing individual SOE or IFR withdrawal applications by specific reference number and amount.

 

The total withdrawals under the SOE or IFR procedures should be part of the overall reconciliation of Bank disbursements described in paragraph 5 above.

 

7.         DESIGNATED ACCOUNT

In conjunction with the audit of the Project PFSs, the auditor is also required to review the activities of the Designated Account associated with the project.  The Designated Account usually comprises:

 

-           Advance deposits received from World Bank;

-           Replenishments substantiated by withdrawal applications;

-           Interest that may have been earned on the accounts, and which belong to      

            the recipient; and

-           Withdrawals related to project expenditures

The auditor should pay particular attention as to the compliance with the Bank's procedures and the balances of the Designated Accounts at the end of the fiscal year (or period). The auditor should examine the eligibility of financial transactions during the period under examination and fund balances at the end of such a period, the operation and use of the DAs in accordance with the relevant general conditions, relevant financing agreements, and disbursement letter, and the adequacy of internal controls for this type of disbursement mechanism. 

For this Project, the Designated Accounts are referred to in the general conditions, the Financing Agreement (subsection 5.3), and the Disbursement Letter (para. I).

The auditor should also examine the eligibility and correctness of:

 

  • Financial transactions during the period under review;

 

  • Account balances at the end of such a period;

 

  • The operation and use of the Designated Account in accordance with the financing agreement; and

 

  • The adequacy of internal controls for the type of disbursement mechanism.

 

8.   AUDITORS' EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS

The audit firm should be registered as authorized to practice in Nigeria and have partners with practice licenses from a national professional accountancy body with IFAC membership. The firm should have relevant experience in accounting and auditing of development projects, especially donor-funded operations.

 

8.0       DELIVERABLES

 

8.1       AUDIT REPORT

The auditor will issue an opinion on the project financial statements (PFSs). The annual audit report of the project accounts should include a separate paragraph highlighting key internal control weaknesses and non-compliance with the financing agreement terms.

 

The auditor will, in addition, provide a special opinion on the expenditures incurred on training/workshop/study tour, identifying any expenditure that is considered ineligible, based on established policy:

Special Opinion

Rationale

Use of Funds by project and non-project staff for travel/training/workshops/study tour.

FM supervision points to systemic non-compliance with policy on retirement of travel advances and doubtful value for money on travel/training/workshops/study tour expenditures. The assessed risk under this category is rated high.

 

 

8.2.      MANAGEMENT LETTER

In addition to the audit report, the auditor will prepare a management letter, in which the auditor will:

 

(a)   Give comments and observations on the accounting records, systems and controls that were examined during the course of the audit;

 

(b)   Identify specific deficiencies or areas of weakness in systems and controls, and make recommendations for their improvement;

 

(c)   Report on the degree of compliance of each of the financial covenants in the financing agreement and give comments, if any, on internal and external matters affecting such compliance;

 

  1. Communicate matters that have come to his/her attention during the audit which might have a significant impact on the implementation of the project;

 

  1. Give comments on the extent to which outstanding issues/qualifications issues have been addressed;

 

  1. Give comments on previous audits’ recommendations that have not been satisfactorily implemented; and

 

  1. Bring to the recipient’s attention any other matters that the auditor considers pertinent, including ineligible expenditures.

 

Ideally, the management letter should also include responses from the implementing agency to the issues highlighted by the auditor.

 

9.         AVAILABLE INFORMATION

The auditor should have access to all legal documents, correspondence, and any other information associated with the project and deemed necessary by the auditor. The auditor will also obtain confirmation of amounts disbursed and outstanding at the Bank. Available information should include copies of the relevant: project appraisal document; financing agreement; financial management assessment reports; supervision mission reports, and implementation status reports.

 

10.       GENERAL

The financial statements, including the audit report, management letter, and management response, should be received by the Bank no later than xxxx months after the end of the accounting year to which the audit relates. 

 

The auditor should submit the report to the recipient’s designated agent rather than to any staff member of the project entity.  The agent should then promptly forward two copies of the audit report and accompanying statements to the Bank, together with the management letter and management response.

 

The auditor should become familiar with the Bank’s Guidelines on Annual Financial Reporting for World Bank-Financed Activities, June 30, 2003, which summarizes the Bank’s financial reporting and auditing requirements. The auditor should be familiar with World Bank Procurement Guidelines, which can be obtained from the project implementing agency. The auditor should also be familiar with the Bank’s Disbursement Handbook for World Bank Clients, Disbursement Guidelines for Projects: May 2006. These documents are available on the Bank’s website and could be obtained from the Task Team Leader.

procnotices.contact_address: NDjamena
procnotices.notice_text:
SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET

 

NOM DU PAYS : TCHAD

NOM DU PROJET : PROJET DE DÉVELOPPEMENT ET D’ACCÈS AU FINANCEMENT DES MICROS PETITES ET MOYENNES ENTREPRISES AU TCHAD                                        

SELECTION D’UN CABINET CHARGÉ DE L’ÉTUDE SUR LA CRÉATION D’UN FONDS DE GARANTIE POUR L’ACCÈS AU FINANCEMENT DES PETITES ET MOYENNES ENTREPRISES

N° de Don : Don IDA-E6040-TD

Non. de référence : Projet MPME- P182134.

Le Gouvernement de la République du Tchad, avec l’appui financier de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) du Groupe de la Banque mondiale et travers le Projet d’harmonisation et d’amélioration des statistiques en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (PHASOC ayant abrité le fonds de préparation du Projet de Développement et d’Accès au Financement des Micro, Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (MPME), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce don pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : Sélection d’un cabinet chargé de l’étude sur la création d’un fonds de garantie pour l’accès au financement des Petites et Moyennes Entreprises.

L’objectif général de la mission est de conduire la mise en place du Fonds National de Garantie destiné à améliorer l’accès des micros, petites et moyennes entreprises (MPME) au financement au Tchad. Ce travail va inclure la conception du modèle institutionnel, juridique, financier et opérationnel et devra permettre de définir un mécanisme de garantie efficace, durable et conforme aux bonnes pratiques internationales en matière de dispositifs publics de garantie, tout en tenant compte du cadre juridique et réglementaire applicable dans la zone CEMAC, notamment les dispositions de l’OHADA et les exigences prudentielles de la Commission Bancaire de l’Afrique Centrale (COBAC).

Le fonds de garantie aura pour vocation de réduire le risque supporté par les institutions financières dans le financement des PME, en apportant des garanties partielles sur les prêts accordés aux entreprises, afin de stimuler l’offre de crédit au secteur privé et de favoriser la croissance des entreprises.

De manière spécifique, la mission visera à :

  • Analyser les contraintes d’accès au financement des PME ;
  • Concevoir le modèle institutionnel du fonds :
  • Définir le cadre juridique et réglementaire :
  • Concevoir les produits de garantie ;  
  • Élaborer le modèle financier du fonds ;
  • Préparer et suivre le dossier d’agrément auprès de la COBAC.

 

Les termes de référence (TDR) de la mission pourront être obtenus à l’adresse ci-dessous mentionnée.

L’Institut National de la Statistique des Études Économiques et Démographiques, à travers la Coordination Nationale du Projet PHASAOC, invite les Candidats (« Consultants ») admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des services. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont : (i) le domaine d’activités de la firme de consultant et le nombre d’années d’expérience générale en matière d’audits depuis la création ; (ii) les expériences similaires réalisées dans le cadre de l’étude sur la création d’un fonds de garantie pour l’accès au financement des Petites et Moyennes Entreprises avec des projets de développement financés par des bailleurs multilatéraux et/ou bilatéraux ; (iii) les preuves des capacités organisationnelles dans les domaines administratifs et techniques.

 

Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants que les dispositions des paragraphes 3.14 ; 3.16 et 3.17 de la Section III du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement – édition de Juillet 2016 et modifié en Septembre 2025 relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts s’appliquent.

Un Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode « Sélection fondée sur les qualifications des consultants » telle que décrite dans le « Règlement ».

Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires tous les jours ouvrables à l’adresse ci-dessous et aux heures suivantes : Du lundi au jeudi de 8 h 00 à 15 h 00 et le vendredi de 08 h 00 à 12 h 00. Date limite de dépôt des dossiers : le 25 mai 2026.

Les manifestations d’intérêt écrites doivent être déposées à l’adresse ci-dessous sous plis fermés, en mentionnant le choix du poste, tout en indiquant « à ne pas ouvrir avant le 25 mai 2026 » à 14 h 30 mn aux adresses ci-dessous.

République Du Sénégal

Un Peuple – Un But – Une Foi

 

Ministère de l’Education nationale

PROJET D’AMELIORATION DES PERFORMANCES

DU SYSTEME EDUCATIF (PAPSE)

Financement :

APPEL A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET (AMI) SN-MEN-542773-CS-QCBS/C_PAPSE_215

 

RECRUTEMENT D'UN CABINET POUR L'ETUDE DE FAISABILITE ET ELABORATION DU CAHIER DES CHARGES POUR LA MISE EN PLACE D’UN SYSTEME DE GESTION ET D’INTELLIGENCE CURRICULAIRE (CIMS)

Pays

République du Sénégal

Emprunteur

République du Sénégal

Secteur

Ministère de l’Education nationale (MEN)

Nom du Projet

Projet d’Amélioration des Performances du système Educatif (PAPSE)

Numéro du Projet

P169916

Mode de Financement

Crédit IDA 70440-SN 

Unité de Gestion du Projet (UGP)

Coordination PAPSE

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

  1. Le Sénégal a obtenu dans le secteur de l’Education un financement de la Banque mondiale d'un montant équivalant à cent millions (100 000 000) $ USD pour financer le Projet d’Amélioration des Performances du Système Educatif (PAPSE), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce crédit pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant « Sélection d'une firme pour l'intégration des API de paiements à la plateforme sécurisée de paiement de la Banque mondiale. ».

2. Les services de consultant (« Services ») permettront d’évaluer la faisabilité technique, fonctionnelle, institutionnelle, organisationnelle et financière de la mise en place d’un CIMS au service de la refondation curriculaire nationale, et produire, sur cette base, un cahier des charges fonctionnel et technique opérationnel pour sa mise en œuvre progressive.

De façon spécifique, il s’agit de:

  • clarifier le périmètre fonctionnel d’un moteur curriculaire intelligent adapté au contexte sénégalais ;
  • identifier les scénarios possibles de mise en œuvre (développement, adaptation, acquisition, mutualisation) ;
  • proposer un phasage progressif réaliste ;
  • analyser les exigences techniques et architecturales minimales ;
  • examiner les options de gouvernance et d’appropriation institutionnelle ;
  • évaluer la soutenabilité financière et organisationnelle à moyen et long terme ;
  • identifier les risques, contraintes et facteurs clés de réussite ;
  • formuler des recommandations opérationnelles pour la décision publique ;
  • élaborer un cahier des charges fonctionnel et technique détaillé du CIMS, sur la base des conclusions de l’étude de faisabilité ; et
  • proposer un phasage opérationnel de la mise en œuvre, y compris les jalons, les priorités et une estimation du budget par phase.

3. Le Coordonnateur du Projet d’Amélioration des Performances du Système Educatif (PAPSE) invite les cabinets (« Consultants ») admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils disposent des qualifications requises et de l’expérience pertinente pour l’exécution desdits services. À ce titre, les dossiers de manifestation d’intérêt devront comporter au moins : (i) une présentation générale du cabinet (brochures, statut juridique, etc.) ; (ii) des références pertinentes concernant l’exécution de missions similaires, dûment justifiées ; (iii) une description de l’expérience générale et spécifique du cabinet, incluant le nombre d’années d’expérience ; (iv) une présentation de l’organisation managériale et technique, y compris l’organigramme, les ressources humaines clés, ainsi que les moyens logistiques et techniques disponibles.

4. Les cabinets intéressés peuvent obtenir les termes de référence (TDR) en envoyant leur demande à l’adresse électronique suivante : bm.papse@education.sn .

5. La liste restreinte comprendra un minimum de trois (3) et un maximum de six (6) cabinets.

6. Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants intéressés que les dispositions relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts telles que décrites dans les paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 et suivants, du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) », daté du 1er Juillet 2016 révisé en septembre 2025, sont applicables.

7. Les Consultants peuvent s’associer à d’autres firmes pour améliorer leurs qualifications, mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’un groupement et/ou d’une sous-traitance. Dans le cas d’un groupement, tous les membres du groupement d’entreprises seront solidairement responsables de l’ensemble du contrat, s’ils sont sélectionnés. 

8. Un Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode « Sélection de Consultants Fondée sur la Qualité et sur le Coût (SFQC) » conformément aux dispositions décrites dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés et qui sera expressément énoncé dans la Demande de Propositions (DP).

9. Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations complémentaires à l’adresse suivante : PAPSE, 2ème étage de l’immeuble CAC à Yoff, Cité Biagui, route de l’aéroport Léopold Sédar Senghor-Téléphone : (+221) 33 820 74 71-email : bm.papse@education.sn, tous les jours ouvrables de 9h30mn à 16h30mn TU.

10. Les manifestations d’intérêt écrites doivent être déposées à l’adresse suivante : PAPSE au 2ème étage de l’immeuble CAC à Yoff, Cité Biagui, route de l’aéroport Léopold Sédar Senghor-Téléphone : (+221) 33 820 74 71–ou par email : bm.papse@education.sn, adressé au Coordonnateur du PAPSE, avec la mention « AMI N° SN-MEN-542773-CS-QCBS/C_PAPSE_215- Recrutement d'un cabinet pour l'étude de faisabilité et élaboration du cahier des charges pour la mise en place d’un système de gestion et d’intelligence curriculaire (CIMS)», au plus tard  le mercredi 03 juin 2026 à 10 h00mn TU.

 

                                                                                        Fait à Dakar, le vendredi 15 mai 2026

procnotices.notice_text:
Request for Expression of Interest (REOI) COUNTRY: Republic of Lebanon PROJECT NAME: Fiscal Management Project (FMP) (P181155) CONSULTING SERVICES: Junior SIGTAS/Oracle Developer/IT Assistant DUTY STATION: Ministry of Finance

1. The Government of Lebanon has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Fiscal Management Project (FMP) (P181155). The Ministry of Finance (MoF) is seeking to use part of the proceeds of the funds to finance 4 positions of Junior SIGTAS/Oracle Developer/IT Assistant.

2. The Junior SIGTAS/Oracle Developer / IT Assistant(s) will have the primary responsibility to support day-to-day technical operations related to legacy tax systems, including SIGTAS/Oracle system support, data validation and reconciliation, reporting support, digital services support, and contribution to future Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS) readiness.

3. Responsibilities: The Junior SIGTAS/Oracle Developer/IT Assistant(s) will support system operations under the supervision of the Project Manager/Coordinator and the Senior SIGTAS/Oracle Developer, and in coordination with relevant directorates within the Ministry of Finance. The Consultant will assist in monitoring SIGTAS availability and performance; identifying and resolving minor system issues; performing routine system checks and validations; supporting data validation and reconciliation between SIGTAS, Treasury systems, and e-services; verifying VAT transactions, including declarations and payments; generating routine reports and statistical outputs; assisting in the compilation of management information; supporting e-payment and online taxpayer service processes; coordinating with internal teams on operational issues; participating in training on tax administration systems, databases, and digital services; documenting workflows and procedures; and contributing to future ITAS readiness through technical support and capacity development.

4. Duration: The contract duration will be for one year, renewable based on satisfactory performance, availability of funds and project needs.

5. Selection Criteria: The selection shall be based on the qualifications, experience, and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience, and skills should include:  Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field.  One to three (1–3) years of relevant experience in IT or database systems.  Basic knowledge of SQL and database management.  Familiarity with Oracle systems is an advantage.  Understanding of financial or tax systems is a plus.  Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.  Ability to work in a team and follow instructions.  Fluency in Arabic and English; French is an advantage.

6. The MoF now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above mentioned services. Interested consultants must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the Services and furnish their Curriculum Vitae (CV) and motivation letter.

7. The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers September 2025 [Procurement in Investment Project Financing; Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services], setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

8. A consultant will be selected in accordance with the procedures set out in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers September 2025 for the selection of individual consultants.

9. Interested Consultants may obtain further information at the address given below from 9:00 to 14:00 hours (Beirut local time) on working days (Monday through Friday) or by consulting the Terms of Reference published on the MOF website (finance.gov.lb)

10. Deadline for submission: The Expression of Interest (EOI), CV, and motivation letter must be delivered to the address below, in person through a sealed envelope bearing the name of the project and description of the consulting services, or by e-mail, by June 2, 2026, at 14:00 hours (Beirut local time).

Attention: Ministry of Finance Riad El Solh Square Beirut – Lebanon P181155@finance.gov.lb Subject: EOI – Junior SIGTAS/Oracle Developer/IT Assistant – Fiscal Management Project

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)
(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION)

Liberia Investment, Finance and Trade Project (LIFT-P)
Project ID: P171997
Credit Number 7037-LR
Grant Number D9690-LR

May 15, 2026

Individual Consultant as Marketing & Communications Consultant for the National Investment Commission (NIC), LR-MOCI-543060-CS-INDV

The Republic of Liberia through the Ministry of Commerce & Industry has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA)/ World Bank towards the cost of implementing the Liberia Investment, Trade & Finance Project (LIFT-P). The Government of Liberia, through the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, is implementing the Liberia Investment, Finance and Trade (LIFT) Project, a five-year initiative with funding from the World Bank aimed at supporting and promoting economic growth in Liberia. As a foundational project to strengthen the public sector’s ability to facilitate the private sector growth on a sustainable basis, there are ongoing significant efforts devoted to institution-building activities in key agencies, including the National Investment Commission. Additionally, the project supports the strengthening of institutional functioning through needed capacity for Technical Implementing Ministries and Agencies (TIMAs). LIFT’s main objective is to improve the investment climate, expand sustainable access to finance, and increase the efficiency of trade in Liberia.

As part of such technical assistance, the National Investment Commission has approached the LIFT Project that it is looking to expand its investment promotion efforts to larger markets with investors that have the potential for expansion, improve its capacity to effectively promote investment and attract foreign investment, and conduct a comprehensive analysis of major economic sectors, including Fishery/Aquaculture, Tourism, Infrastructure (Road, Seaport, Airport, Rail & ICT), Mining, Health, Transportation/Logistic, Energy and Manufacturing, etc. It is predicated upon this that the NIC is seeking an expert in investment marketing and communication to design and develop its marketing and communication strategies including investment promotional materials under its Lead Generation and Investment Promotion Programs to attract investors.

To support this ambition, NIC is seeking a Marketing and Communications Consultant to lead and execute a communications-focused strategy that strengthens brand positioning, promotes Liberia’s investment opportunities, and supports lead generation through storytelling and strategic media engagement.

Key Objectives of the Assignment 

The Key Objective of the consultancy is to develop and implement a strategic communication plan that enhances Liberia’s investment brand, builds stakeholder trust, and supports the NIC’s investor targeting and outreach goals.

Scope of the Assignment

The Consultant will undertake the following key tasks:

A. Strategic Communications Planning

  • Develop and execute a Communications & Media Strategy aligned with NIC’s investment promotion priorities.
  • Create key messaging frameworks for Liberia’s priority investment sectors (agriculture, tourism, renewable energy, infrastructure, etc.).
  • Establish and maintain a quarterly editorial calendar aligned with investor engagement goals and missions.

B. Content Development & Storytelling

  • Produce compelling multimedia content (articles, investor briefs, blog posts, sector profiles, infographics, videos) for both domestic and international investor audiences.
  • Coordinate the development of Liberia's “Investment Opportunity” brochures, sector pitch decks, and success stories.
  • Write and distribute press releases, op-eds, and feature stories that highlight Liberia’s investment reforms and ongoing investor engagements.

C. Digital & Media Engagement

  • Oversee the revamp and ongoing content updates of NIC’s official website and social media channels (LinkedIn, X, Facebook, YouTube).
  • Develop a monthly investor newsletter to share updates, reforms, opportunities, and success stories.
  • Lead the development of the 6th edition of the Investor’s Guide to Liberia

D. Event & Campaign Support

  • Provide communications support for investment missions, trade expos, and investor roadshows.
  • Develop investor mission briefing kits, talking points, media kits, and post-event reports.
  • Support brand visibility through creative campaign materials and event-related media content.

E. Internal Capacity Support

  • Train NIC staff on messaging, media engagement, and digital storytelling.
  • Develop a Branding Style Guide for the Investment Promotion team.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can found at the link below: hppt //: www.moci.gov.lr  / www.emansion.gov.lr / www.nic.gov.lr

The Ministry of Commerce and Industry now invites eligible Individual Consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Individual Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are listed as per the Terms of Reference provided below. The Consultant should have minimum qualifications and experience as follows:

  • Bachelor’s degree in communication/branding with at least 7 years of experience in marketing, PR, or communications - preferably within investment promotion, international development, or government.
  • Master’s degree is an added advantage.
  • Demonstrated experience creating compelling positive narratives
  • Strong writing, editing, and visual storytelling skills
  • Experience with social media strategy, and website content management,
  • Familiarity with Liberia’s socio-economic and political landscape is a plus
  • Demonstrated experience in facilitation and reporting results.
  • Highly motivated and committed to institutional values of professionalism, accountability, integrity and teamwork, organizational development / or management.
  • Strong experience in the use of computers (word, Excel, PowerPoint, Publisher, etc);

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated July 2016, Revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, September 2023, February 2025 and September 2025  (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.    

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection (INDV) method set out in the Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016 as Revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, September 2023, February 2025 and September 2025).

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, i.e., 0900 to 1600 hours GMT, Monday to Friday.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (only by email) on or before Friday May 29, 2026, with subject:          “ Marketing & Communications Consultant for the National Investment Commission (NIC), LR-MOCI-543060-CS-INDV”.

Background

The Government of Liberia, through the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, is implementing the Liberia Investment, Finance and Trade (LIFT) Project, a five-year initiative with funding from the World Bank aimed at supporting and promoting economic growth in Liberia. As a foundational project to strengthen the public sector’s ability to facilitate the private sector growth on a sustainable basis, there are ongoing significant efforts devoted to institution-building activities in key agencies, including the National Investment Commission. Additionally, the project supports the strengthening of institutional functioning through needed capacity for Technical Implementing Ministries and Agencies (TIMAs). LIFT’s main objective is to improve the investment climate, expand sustainable access to finance, and increase the efficiency of trade in Liberia.

As part of such technical assistance, the National Investment Commission has approached the LIFT Project that it is looking to expand its investment promotion efforts to larger markets with investors that have the potential for expansion, improve its capacity to effectively promote investment and attract foreign investment, and conduct a comprehensive analysis of major economic sectors, including Fishery/Aquaculture, Tourism, Infrastructure (Road, Seaport, Airport, Rail & ICT), Mining, Health, Transportation/Logistic, Energy and Manufacturing, etc. It is predicated upon this that the NIC is seeking an expert in investment marketing and communication to design and develop its marketing and communication strategies including investment promotional materials under its Lead Generation and Investment Promotion Programs to attract investors.  

Description of the Assignment

The National Investment Commission is responsible for promoting and facilitating foreign direct investment (FDI) and improving the investment climate. As part of its renewed investment drive, the NIC seeks to significantly enhance its visibility, articulate Liberia’s value proposition more effectively, and develop compelling narratives that position the country as a prime investment destination.

To support this ambition, NIC is seeking a Marketing and Communications Consultant to lead and execute a communications-focused strategy that strengthens brand positioning, promotes Liberia’s investment opportunities, and supports lead generation through storytelling and strategic media engagement.

The Key Objective of the consultancy is to develop and implement a strategic communication plan that enhances Liberia’s investment brand, builds stakeholder trust, and supports the NIC’s investor targeting and outreach goals.

3. Scope of Work

The Consultant will undertake the following key tasks:

A. Strategic Communications Planning

  • Develop and execute a Communications & Media Strategy aligned with NIC’s investment promotion priorities.
  • Create key messaging frameworks for Liberia’s priority investment sectors (agriculture, tourism, renewable energy, infrastructure, etc.).
  • Establish and maintain a quarterly editorial calendar aligned with investor engagement goals and missions.

B. Content Development & Storytelling

  • Produce compelling multimedia content (articles, investor briefs, blog posts, sector profiles, infographics, videos) for both domestic and international investor audiences.
  • Coordinate the development of Liberia's “Investment Opportunity” brochures, sector pitch decks, and success stories.
  • Write and distribute press releases, op-eds, and feature stories that highlight Liberia’s investment reforms and ongoing investor engagements.

C. Digital & Media Engagement

  • Oversee the revamp and ongoing content updates of NIC’s official website and social media channels (LinkedIn, X, Facebook, YouTube).
  • Develop a monthly investor newsletter to share updates, reforms, opportunities, and success stories.
  • Lead the development of the 6th edition of the Investor’s Guide to Liberia

D. Event & Campaign Support

  • Provide communications support for investment missions, trade expos, and investor roadshows.
  • Develop investor mission briefing kits, talking points, media kits, and post-event reports.
  • Support brand visibility through creative campaign materials and event-related media content.

E. Internal Capacity Support

  • Train NIC staff on messaging, media engagement, and digital storytelling.
  • Develop a Branding Style Guide for the Investment Promotion team.

4. Deliverables

Deliverable

Description

Timeline

% of Total Contract Amount

1. Inception Report & Communications Strategy + Branding Style Guide

3. 6th Edition Investor’s Guide to Liberia (Final)

4. Digital Platforms Revamp & Activation and Content Performance Report

Updated NIC website (content + structure), and active social media platforms (LinkedIn, X, Facebook, YouTube) with consistent branding and initial content rollout 

Delivery of 3 months of content (newsletters, blogs, press releases), media engagement outputs, and performance reports

6. Communications SOP & Staff Training Report

Communications manual, internal SOPs, and report on staff training conducted

7. Final Report & Consolidated Impact Assessment

Final report covering outputs, performance metrics, lessons learned, and recommendations for sustainability

Day 180

5. Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in communication/branding with at least 7 years of experience in marketing, PR, or communications - preferably within investment promotion, international development, or government.
  • Master’s degree is an added advantage.
  • Demonstrated experience creating compelling positive narratives
  • Strong writing, editing, and visual storytelling skills
  • Experience with social media strategy, and website content management,
  • Familiarity with Liberia’s socio-economic and political landscape is a plus
  • Demonstrated experience in facilitation and reporting results.
  • Highly motivated and committed to institutional values of professionalism, accountability, integrity and teamwork, organizational development / or management.
  • Strong experience in the use of computers (word, Excel, PowerPoint, Publisher, etc);

6.  Approach and Implementation Arrangements

The assignment will be executed by the consultant and will be monitored by the NIC’s focal person (the Director for Investment Promotion) and the LIFT Project Implementation Unit. For reporting purpose, the consultant will submit all drafts and final reports (including monthly report) to the Executive Director of the NIC through the Director for Investment Promotion. The NIC will review all reports and clear before payments are made to the consultant. Additionally, the PIU Focal Persons, the SME and M & E Specialists will also review all reports emanating from the consultant or submitted on behalf of the consultant by the NIC before advising the Project Coordinator to pay to ensure value for money.

Duration of Consultancy

The duration of the assignment is 365 days

Selection Criteria

The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Consultant’s Experience relevant to the Assignment
  • Competency/Qualification of the consultant relevant to the Assignment
  • Recommendations from referees, etc.

procnotices.notice_text:
CALL FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

CONSULTING SERVICES

SELECTION OF FIRMS

Republic of North Macedonia
Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy
Agriculture Modernization Project
Loan No.: 9037-MK

Assignment title: Consulting services for preparation of project-technical documentation — urban planning, conceptual and basic design and Environmental and Social Management Plan — for construction of a Collection and Preparation Center in Strumica.

Reference No.: AMP-CS-CQS-SC1.2-3

The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy of the Republic of North Macedonia has secured financing from the World Bank for the costs of the Agriculture Modernization Project and intends to use part of the funds for payment of consulting services for preparation of project-technical documentation for construction of a Collection and Preparation Center in Strumica.

The Agriculture Modernization Project aims to improve competitiveness in the targeted agricultural subsectors and to strengthen the preparedness of the public agricultural sector for accession to the European Union.

Within Subcomponent 1.2 – Agricultural and Food Products Distribution Systems, the Project supports the construction of modern, efficient and sustainable post-harvest infrastructure with the aim of improving value chains and access to markets for agricultural producers. Key investments within this subcomponent include the development of the logistics-distribution center in Skopje and the construction of Collection and Preparation Centers, including the Collection and Preparation Center in Strumica.

The Collection and Preparation Center in Strumica will be located in the village of Kuklish, Municipality of Strumica, on state agricultural land — cadastral parcel CP 2853/1 — which provides sufficient space for development of the required infrastructure and possibility for future expansion.

The Collection and Preparation Center in Strumica is conceived as a modern post-harvest facility, designed to improve handling, storage and placement of agricultural products. The facility will provide services such as sorting, classification, packaging, pre-cooling, cold storage and logistical support, thereby reducing post-harvest losses, improving the quality of products and facilitating access to domestic and export markets.

Based on the prepared Feasibility Study for the Collection and Preparation Center in Strumica and the accompanying documentation, the main facility is planned with dimensions of 70 m × 48 m, as a compact, linear facility with a total area of approximately 3,360 m². Outside the facility, an internal yard, parking and maneuvering area of at least 4,000 m² are planned, as well as access roads, green protective belts and space for possible future technical installations.

The objective of the assignment is to provide support to the institution for implementation of the Project in the preparation of complete and harmonized project-technical documentation for construction of the Collection and Preparation Center in Strumica, located at the selected location in the village of Kuklish — cadastral parcel CP 2853/1.

The assignment includes preparation of a Basic Design and an Environmental and Social Management Plan — ESMP — in accordance with the applicable national legal regulation and the Environmental and Social Framework of the World Bank.

The results of this assignment will serve as the basis for obtaining construction approval from the Municipality of Strumica and will ensure that the Project is technically sound, aligned with environmental and social requirements and ready for implementation.

More details about the assignment are given in the Terms of Reference, which is an integral part of this Call.

The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy now invites eligible consulting firms, hereinafter referred to as “Consultants”, to express their interest in providing the services.

Interested Consultants should submit information showing that they possess the required qualifications, relevant experience and capacity to perform the services. The submitted information will be used for assessment of the qualifications and relevant experience of the Consultants and for preparation of a shortlist, in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection method — CQS.

At this stage, submission of a technical proposal, methodology, financial proposal or price is not required. After completion of the evaluation of the submitted expressions of interest, the most suitably qualified Consultant will be invited to submit a technical and financial proposal for negotiations.

Description of the services

The Consultant will carry out all activities necessary for preparation of the project-technical documentation and the environmental and social protection instruments necessary for construction of the Collection and Preparation Center in Strumica. The assignment is structured in two mutually connected phases:

• Phase I: Preparation of Basic Design.

• Phase II: Preparation of Environmental and Social Management Plan.

Phase I will include preparation of a location-specific conceptual design, preparation of a design for an access road that will connect the location with the local Kuklish–Bansko road, preparation of Basic Design, provision of support to the Client in obtaining construction approval from the Municipality of Strumica, and technical assistance — extended designer’s services during implementation of the works contract.

The Basic Design will cover all relevant engineering disciplines, including architectural design, structural design, construction and ground works, electrical design, photovoltaic system design, mechanical — HVAC — design, water supply and sewerage design, sprinkler system design, traffic design and additional documentation foreseen by the national regulation.

Approval of the location-specific conceptual design by the Client, after consultations with the relevant users/stakeholders, will be a precondition for moving towards preparation of the Basic Design.

Phase II will include preparation of a location-specific Environmental and Social Management Plan — ESMP — for the construction and operation of the Collection and Preparation Center in Strumica, in full compliance with the Project Environmental and Social Management Framework, the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework, the World Bank Group Environmental, Health and Safety Guidelines and the applicable national regulation.

The Consultant, in addition to the World Bank requirements for environmental and social aspects, will also comply with the national environmental requirements and, if necessary, will prepare an Environmental Protection Elaborate.

The ESMP will include identification and consultations with stakeholders, at least one public hearing, a grievance mechanism, monitoring and reporting measures, emergency procedures, as well as integration of the environmental and social measures into the technical specifications, bills of quantities and design solutions.

Delivery and timeline

Phase / delivery No. Deliverables Deadline for submission Client’s comments
Phase I / D1 Basic Design package 45 days after signing of the contract 7 days after submission
Phase II / D2 Environmental and Social Management Plan 30 days after signing of the contract 7 days after submission

* Calendar days

Final approval of all deliverables will be given within 5 days after receipt of the version that fully addresses the Client’s comments and is accepted by the Client. All reports should be prepared in Macedonian language.

Information to be submitted

For assessment of qualifications, experience and capacity, interested Consultants should submit short and relevant information which, as a minimum, should contain the following:

short profile of the Consultant, including basic information on legal status, organization, main activity, years of experience and areas of specialization;

information on the Consultant’s general experience in preparation of project-technical documentation;

information on relevant specific experience in preparation of structural or basic design for industrial facilities, warehouses, logistics capacities or agro-food facilities, industrial zones or similar capacities;

reference list of similar projects/contracts implemented in the last 5 — five — years, containing description of the services provided, contract value, client, location/country, duration, assignment budget, percentage of participation of the Consultant in case of association/subcontracting and main activities;

certificates/confirmations for successfully completed contracts and examples of assignments of similar nature;

information on fulfilment of the applicable legal, licensing and professional conditions for performing the subject services, including valid License B for preparation of design documentation, issued in accordance with the national legislation of the Republic of North Macedonia; foreign firms may obtain information at: http://mtc.gov.mk;

information on experience in working in the Balkan region, if such experience exists;

information on the available professional and organizational capacity of the Consultant for preparation of Basic Design, ESMP, technical specifications, bills of quantities, drawings, professional review and support in the construction approval procedure;

short information on the proposed or available structure of the expert team, especially in relation to team leader/designer, designer and environmental and social expert;

information on other non-key experts required in accordance with the nature and scope of the services and the available professional capacity of the Consultant, if such experts are foreseen;

information on possible experience in projects financed by international financial institutions, especially the World Bank, if such experience exists;

statement on potential conflict of interest, if any exists, or confirmation that the Consultant is not aware of the existence of circumstances that could represent a conflict of interest in relation to the subject assignment;

in case of expression of interest by a joint venture, consortium or other type of association, clear indication of the structure of the association, the leading partner, the roles and responsibilities of each member, as well as information whether certain activities would be carried out through subconsultants.

The information should be short, clear and directly related to the subject of the assignment. Consultants are not required at this stage to submit a full technical proposal, financial proposal or detailed methodology. The Ministry reserves the right to request additional clarifications or evidence from the Consultants, if this is necessary for verification of the submitted information and for the purposes of evaluation of qualifications.

Minimum qualification expectations

Interested Consultants should demonstrate that they have relevant experience and capacity to perform the services, especially in the following areas:

• at least 5 — five — years of relevant experience in preparation of project-technical documentation;

• at least 5 — five — implemented similar contracts in the last 5 — five — years for structural or basic design for industrial facilities, warehouses, logistics capacities or agro-food facilities, industrial zones or similar capacities;

• valid License B for preparation of design documentation, issued in accordance with the national legislation of the Republic of North Macedonia;

• experience in working in the Balkan region, which will be considered an advantage;

• institutional and professional capacity for preparation of location-specific conceptual design, Basic Design, ESMP, technical specifications, bills of quantities, drawings and other documentation foreseen by the national regulation;

• ability to provide complete professional review and positive opinion from a licensed company authorized to perform such review;

• availability of an appropriate expert team with experience in urban planning, preparation of design documentation and construction/supervision/management of warehouses, logistics or agro-food facilities.

Key experts

The basic team of the Consultant is expected to include the following key experts:

• Team leader/designer: higher education in civil engineering or architecture — master studies will be considered an advantage; authorized designer — License B; minimum 10 years of proven professional experience in designing public, industrial or residential facilities; chief designer in at least 5 similar assignments; experience with FIDIC design standards.

• Designer: higher education in civil engineering or architecture; authorized designer — License B; minimum 7 years of proven professional experience in designing public, industrial or residential facilities; at least 4 similar design assignments, of which 2 as chief designer; experience with FIDIC standards.

• Environmental and social expert: higher education in environmental engineering, environmental sciences, environmental management, social sciences, sociology or related fields; minimum 10 years of experience in assessment of environmental and social impacts, preferably in developing countries; knowledge of the World Bank safeguard policies and the Environmental and Social Framework — ESF — will be considered an advantage; experience in the agricultural sector and natural resources management will be considered an advantage.

Criteria for assessment of expressions of interest

The submitted expressions of interest will be reviewed and evaluated based on the relevance and quality of the submitted information. The evaluation will be carried out with the aim of determining the Consultants with the most suitable qualifications and references for performance of the assignment and for preparation of a shortlist.

Assessment criterion Maximum number of points
General experience and institutional capacity of the Consultant in preparation of project-technical documentation 20
Specific experience in similar assignments for structural or basic design for industrial facilities, warehouses, logistics capacities, agro-food facilities, industrial zones or similar capacities 35
Relevant experience in preparation of complete basic designs, technical specifications, bills of quantities, professional review, support for construction approval and environmental and social instruments 20
Fulfilment of applicable legal, licensing, professional and institutional conditions for performing the subject services, including valid License B for preparation of design documentation 15
Organizational capacity and availability of relevant professional team 10
Total 100

The evaluation at this stage will be based on the submitted qualification information and references. Technical methodology, detailed work plan or financial proposal will not be evaluated, because they are not subject of this stage of the procedure.

The Ministry reserves the right not to proceed with the next stage if none of the submitted expressions of interest shows sufficiently relevant qualifications, experience and capacity to perform the assignment.

Selection method

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection method — CQS — in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for Borrowers under Investment Project Financing.

In accordance with this method, the Ministry prepares the Terms of Reference, then requests expressions of interest and qualification information on the experience and competence of the Consultants relevant to the assignment. Based on the submitted information, the Ministry will prepare a shortlist of Consultants that may be invited to submit proposals in the next stage of the procedure, in accordance with the applicable World Bank procurement rules.

Conflict of interest

The attention of interested Consultants is directed to the applicable provisions of the World Bank Procurement Regulations in relation to conflict of interest.

Consultants should provide professional, objective and impartial advice and should at all times keep in mind the interest of the Client. Consultants should avoid conflict with other assignments, their own business interests or interests of related persons that may affect their independence and objectivity.

Interested Consultants should state whether there are circumstances that could represent a potential or real conflict of interest in relation to the subject assignment. Failure to declare a relevant conflict of interest may constitute grounds for exclusion from further consideration.

Association of consultants

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture, consortium or subconsultancy arrangement with the aim of strengthening their qualifications.

In case of a joint venture or consortium, all members will be evaluated jointly for the purposes of the qualification assessment and their combined relevant experience and capacity will be taken into account. If the contract is awarded to a joint venture or consortium, the members of such association will be jointly and severally liable for performance of the assignment, unless the applicable rules or contractual conditions provide otherwise.

Interested Consultants should clearly state the structure of the association, the leading partner, the roles and responsibilities of each partner and subconsultant, as well as the part of the assignment expected to be performed by each of them.

Unclear formulations such as “in cooperation with”, “in connection with”, “with support from” or similar expressions, without clear indication of the structure, roles and responsibilities, may not be taken into account during the evaluation.

As a principle, one firm may submit only one expression of interest, independently or as a member of a joint venture or consortium. A firm that submits an expression of interest independently or as a member of a joint venture or consortium should not simultaneously participate as a subconsultant in another expression of interest in the same procedure. A firm may participate as a subconsultant in more than one expression of interest, provided that it does not submit an independent expression of interest and is not a member of a joint venture or consortium in the same procedure.

Language of the expression of interest

The expression of interest and the accompanying information should be submitted in Macedonian language or in English language. If certain references, confirmations or accompanying information are available in another language, the Consultant may submit a short translation or summary in Macedonian or English language.

Deadline and manner of submission

Expressions of interest must be submitted in written form to the address indicated below, in person, by mail or by electronic mail, no later than:

Tuesday, 02 June 2026, by 15:00 hours local time

Expressions of interest submitted after the expiry of the indicated deadline may not be taken into account.

Address for submission and contact

Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy
Agriculture Modernization Project
Contact person: Ms. Ana Gaceva
“Amintha Treti” St. No. 2
1000 Skopje
Republic of North Macedonia
e-mail: procurement@amp.mk

Additional information may be obtained at the above-mentioned address during working hours from 08:00 to 16:00 hours, local time.

Note

This Call for Expressions of Interest does not constitute a request for technical or financial proposal and does not create an obligation for the Ministry to conclude a contract with any of the interested Consultants.

The Ministry reserves the right, in accordance with the applicable World Bank procurement rules, to request additional information or clarifications from the Consultants, not to proceed with the procedure if the submitted expressions of interest do not show a sufficiently qualified market response, or to continue the procedure in accordance with the applicable selection method.

Request for Expression of Interest (REOI) COUNTRY: PROJECT NAME: Republic of Lebanon Fiscal Management Project (FMP) (P181155) CONSULTING SERVICES: Senior SIGTAS/Oracle Developer/IT Specialist DUTY STATION: Ministry of Finance

1. The Government of Lebanon has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Fiscal Management Project (FMP) (P181155). The Ministry of Finance (MOF) is seeking to use part of the proceeds of the funds to finance 2 positions of Senior SIGTAS/Oracle Developer / IT Specialist.

2. The Senior SIGTAS/Oracle Developer/IT Specialist will support the Ministry of Finance in ensuring the stable and reliable operation of SIGTAS, including system performance, data quality, reconciliation, reporting, e-payment and interface support, and digital taxpayer services. The Consultant will also provide senior technical assistance for system maintenance, operational improvements, and preparation for migration and transition toward the future Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS).

3. Responsibilities: The Senior SIGTAS/Oracle Developer/IT Specialist(s) will support the Ministry of Finance in the stabilization, maintenance, and continuous operation of the current SIGTAS environment, under the supervision of the Project Manager/Coordinator (PM/C) and in coordination with relevant MoF directorates. The role includes ensuring the continuous operation and stability of SIGTAS, particularly the Revenue and VAT modules; performing system maintenance, troubleshooting, and performance optimization; overseeing database integrity, including backup, recovery, and user management; implementing approved parameter changes, configurations, and technical adjustments related to tax procedures and business rules; supporting optimization of Revenue and VAT administration processes, including exemptions, reassessments, and payment arrangements; preparing technical reports, queries, scripts, and operational tools required for continuity, controls, and management reporting; supporting testing and validation of approved system changes; supporting and enhancing e-payment systems and online tax services; ensuring connectivity between SIGTAS and external platforms, including banks, payment gateways, Treasury, and other MoF systems; enhancing payment allocation and reconciliation mechanisms; leading reconciliation processes between SIGTAS, Treasury systems, and e-services; ensuring data consistency and integrity across systems; developing tools for automated reconciliation and data validation; supporting data migration and data cleaning activities when required; generating Revenue and VAT statistics financial reports, and analytical outputs; providing reporting support for IMF, World Bank, and other stakeholders; coordinating with MOF departments, external stakeholders, banks, and service providers; providing guidance and supervision to junior developers; contributing to ITAS transition readiness by supporting mapping of existing business processes, data structures, interfaces, and operational requirements; documenting legacy system architecture and migration needs; providing technical inputs for future ITAS procurement, implementation readiness, and transition planning; and supporting knowledge transfer and capacity building within the Ministry.

4. Duration: The assignment will be for a period of one (1) year, with the possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance, availability of funds, and project needs.

5. Selection Criteria: The selection shall be based on the qualifications, experience and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience and skills should include:  Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or related field.  Minimum of fifteen (15) years of experience in software development and database systems.  Extensive experience with Oracle databases, including SQL, PL/SQL, Forms, and Reports.  Proven experience with SIGTAS and tax administration systems.  Strong experience in Revenue and VAT systems, reconciliation, and e-payment processes.  Experience working with Ministry of Finance systems and UNDP projects.  Demonstrated experience in system design, development, and supervision of IT teams.  Experience supporting IMF and World Bank missions.  Strong analytical, problem-solving, and coordination skills.  Experience in system migration or modernization projects is an asset.  Fluency in Arabic and English; French is an asset.

6. The MOF now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above mentioned services. Interested consultants must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the Services and furnish the Curriculum Vitae (CV) and their motivation letter.

7. The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's 'Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers' July 2016 revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, September 2023, February 2025 and September 2025 [Procurement in Investment Project Financing; Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services], setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

8. A consultant will be selected in accordance with the procedures set out in the World Bank's 'Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers' July 2016 revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, September 2023, February 2025 and September 2025 for selection of individual consultant.

9. Interested Consultants may obtain further information at the address given below from 9:00 to 14:00 hours (Beirut local time) on working days (Monday through Friday) or by consulting the Terms of Reference published on the MOF website (finance.gov.lb)

10. UKRAINE

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

Loan Agreement No. 9238-UA; Grant No. TF0C5794

Reference No. MOES-IC-13-MON-2

The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is implementing projects financed by the World Bank, including Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project (UIHERP) and Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine Program (LEARN) Program (hereinafter referred to as the Operations) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. 

The UIHERP aims to increase efficiency and improve conditions to ensure quality and transparency in the higher education system of Ukraine.

LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science’s (MoES) Strategic Action Plan. The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

The objective of this assignment is to provide support to MoES in monitoring and evaluation process for UIHERP and LEARN (hereinafter the Projects), progress in achievement of results indicators including Disbursement linked indicators and results as well as providing the periodic reporting.

procnotices.notice_text:
SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTÉRÊT

NOM DU PAYS : TCHAD

NOM DU PROJET : PROJET DE DÉVELOPPEMENT ET D’ACCÈS AU FINANCEMENT DES MICROS PETITES ET MOYENNES ENTREPRISES AU TCHAD

RECRUTEMENT D’UN CONSULTANT INDIVIDUEL CHARGÉ DE L’ÉLABORATION DU MANUEL D’EXÉCUTION ET D’ADAPTER LE MANUEL HARMONISE DES PROCÉDURES AU CONTEXTE DU PROJET.

N° de Don : Don IDA-E6040-TD

Non. de référence : Projet MPME- P182134.

Le Gouvernement de la République du Tchad, avec l’appui financier de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) du Groupe de la Banque mondiale et travers le Projet d’harmonisation et d’amélioration des statistiques en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (PHASOC) ayant abrité le fonds de préparation du Projet de Développement et d’Accès au Financement des Micro, Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (MPME), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce don pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : Recrutement d’un consultant individuel chargé de l’élaboration du manuel d’exécution et d’adapter le manuel harmonisé des procédures au contexte du Projet.

L’objectif de la mission est d’élaborer deux (2) manuels importants pour le Projet :

(i) le Manuel des procédures d’exécution du projet y inclus les procédures des sauvegardes environnementales et sociales, de communication et de suivi-évaluation. Le document devra contenir une description détaillée des activités prévues, les processus et procédures de leur mise en œuvre et les étapes de contrôle pour la mise en œuvre du projet et les rôles spécifiques des différents acteurs en vue d’atteindre les objectifs de développement. 

(ii) le manuel des procédures administratives, financières, comptables et de passation des marchés y compris des modèles de documents à utiliser (outils de gestion). La mission devra également aboutir à l’élaboration de la charte d’audit interne.

Pour les deux manuels, le Consultant devra assurer la formation des utilisateurs.

Les termes de référence (TDR) de la mission pourront être obtenus à l’adresse ci-dessous mentionnée.

L’Institut National de la Statistique des Études Économiques et Démographiques, à travers la Coordination Nationale du Projet PHASAOC, invite les Candidats (« Consultants ») admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des services. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont : (i) le domaine d’activités de la firme de consultant et le nombre d’années d’expérience générale en matière d’audits depuis la création ; (ii) les expériences similaires réalisées dans l’élaboration des manuels avec des projets de développement financés par des bailleurs multilatéraux et/ou bilatéraux ; (iii) les preuves des capacités organisationnelles dans les domaines administratifs et techniques.

 

Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants que les dispositions des paragraphes 3.14 ; 3.16 et 3.17 de la Section III du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement – édition de Juillet 2016 et modifié en Septembre 2025 relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts s’appliquent.

 

Un Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode « Consultant Individuel » telle que décrite dans le « Règlement ».

Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires tous les jours ouvrables à l’adresse ci-dessous et aux heures suivantes : Du lundi au jeudi de 8 h 00 à 15 h 00 et le vendredi de 08 h 00 à 12 h 00. Date limite de dépôt des dossiers : le 25 mai 2026.

 

Les manifestations d’intérêt écrites doivent être déposées à l’adresse ci-dessous sous plis fermés, en mentionnant le choix du poste, tout en indiquant « à ne pas ouvrir avant le 25 mai 2026 » à 14 h 30 mn aux adresses ci-dessous.
