procnotices.notice_text:
SOLICITUD DE MANIFESTACIÓN DE INTERÉS

(SERVICIOS DE CONSULTORÍA – SELECCIÓN DE EMPRESAS)

PROYECTO DE VÍAS RURALES RESILIENTES DE LA PROVINCIA DEL GUAYAS FINANCIADO CON RECURSOS DEL PRÉSTAMO BIRF No. 9722-EC

CONSULTORÍA DEL DESARROLLO DEL PLAN DE INFRAESTRUCTURA VIAL PROVINCIAL

Consultoría Selección Basada en Calidad y Costo

 

No.: EC-PREFGUAYAS-539311-CS-QCBS

El Gobierno Provincial del Guayas ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para cubrir el costo del PROYECTO DE VÍAS RURALES RESILIENTES DE LA PROVINCIA DEL GUAYAS FINANCIADO CON RECURSOS DEL PRÉSTAMO BIRF No. 9722-EC, y pretende aplicar parte de lo recaudado para servicios de consultoría.

El presente servicio de “CONSULTORÍA DEL DESARROLLO DEL PLAN DE INFRAESTRUCTURA VIAL PROVINCIAL”, tiene como objetivo principal la contratación de una empresa consultora calificada y con experiencia, encargada de elaborar un plan integral que permita la planificación, priorización y gestión eficiente de la red vial provincial, incorporando criterios técnicos, económicos y de resiliencia.

El GOBIERNO PROVINCIAL DEL GUAYAS invita a las empresas/APCA’s y firmas consultoras elegibles que reúnan los requisitos necesarios a presentar su expresión de interés en la presentación de los servicios de consultoría referidos. En esta fase, las empresas/APCA’s deberán presentar: 

1. Carta de interés

Una carta donde se exprese el interés en participar en el proceso, así como la aceptación de las condiciones establecidas en los Términos de Referencia; y,

2. Experiencia de la firma consultora

Información relacionada a la experiencia de la firma consultora:

  1. Experiencia en estudios, consultorías o proyectos relacionados con planificación, gestión de activos o desarrollo de infraestructura vial, ejecutados durante los últimos diez (10) años.

 

b) Experiencia específica que incluya al menos tres  o varios de los siguientes componentes:

  • Elaboración de inventario vial
  • Evaluación de tráfico y demanda vehicular
  • Ejecución de censos de carga en vías
  • Análisis de accesibilidad en entornos urbanos y/o rurales
  • Evaluación funcional y estructural de pavimentos
  • Diseño e implementación de Sistemas de Gestión de Activos Viales

 

Las empresas/APCA’s interesadas deberán adjuntar un resumen de los trabajos y contratos ejecutados con sus respectivos soportes (copia de actas de entrega recepción definitiva, certificado adjuntando la factura con el comprobante de retención, entre otros). Es importante indicar que demuestre la mayor cantidad de experiencia probada. 

 

Nota. Se valorará la experiencia que acrediten una trayectoria sólida en la  ejecución de la mayor cantidad de componentes, en función del nivel de integralidad del servicio.

 

 

Para conocer el alcance de esta contratación, se adjunta los términos de referencia en el siguiente sitio web: https://guayas.gob.ec/vias-rurales-resilientes-en-la-provincia-del- guayasbanco-mundial/ 

 

El plazo de ejecución se establece por etapa de acuerdo a lo detallado en los términos de referencia.

Se solicita a los consultores interesados sobre la Sección III, párrafos, 3.14, 3.16 y 3.17 del "Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión: Adquisiciones en Operaciones de Financiamiento para Proyectos de Inversión: Bienes, Obras, Servicios de NoConsultoría y Servicios de Consultoría (Quinta Edición, septiembre de 2023) y (Sexta edición, febrero 2025, en los casos que corresponda), que establece la política del Banco Mundial sobre conflictos de intereses.

Los consultores pueden asociarse con otras empresas para mejorar sus calificaciones, pero deben indicar claramente si la asociación tiene la forma de una empresa conjunta y/o una sub consultoría. En el caso de una empresa conjunta, todos los socios de la empresa conjunta serán solidariamente responsables de la totalidad del contrato, si son seleccionados.

Se seleccionará a un Consultor de conformidad con el método Selección Basada en Calidad y Costo establecido en el Reglamento de Adquisiciones.

Puede obtener más información en la dirección que se indica a continuación durante el horario de oficina entre las 10h00 y 17h00, de lunes a viernes. 

Las expresiones de interés podrán ser entregadas de manera física y/o electrónica. 

  • Modalidad física: Presentar la expresión de interés firmado de manera electrónica, en una o varias carpetas (conforme lo requiera) junto a un (01) dispositivo de almacenamiento (USB, CD, entre otros).

La información del dispositivo de almacenamiento deberá ser idéntica a los documentos en físico. 

 

Esta información deberá ser entregada en la Dirección de Compras Públicas señalada en la para inferior de este documento, en un (01) sobre cerrado que contenga la siguiente rotulación:

 

Manifestación de Interés

 

Código de Proceso: EC-PREFGUAYAS-539311-CS-QCBS

 

CONSULTORÍA DEL DESARROLLO DEL PLAN DE INFRAESTRUCTURA VIAL PROVINCIAL

Nombre: [incluir el nombre de la empresa/APCA]

 

  • Modalidad Electrónica: Remitir la expresión de interés con firma electrónica a los siguientes correos institucionales: compras.publicas@guayas.gob.ec; adquisiciones.bm@guayas.gob.ec

Por favor considerar que el peso máximo de los archivos que soporta el correo electrónico es de 20 MB, por lo que se recomienda hacer uso de herramientas que no tengan fecha de vencimiento como: one drive, archivos zip, entre otros.

La manifestación de interés deberá ser remitida hasta el 29 de abril de 2026, 15h00.

Description of Services

Tanzania’s coral reef ecosystems are among the most biologically diverse and economically valuable marine habitats in Marine Parks and Reserves in Tanzania. Reef-associated fisheries provide critical livelihoods, food security, and income for coastal communities. However, these resources face increasing threats from overfishing, habitat degradation, climate change, unregulated practices, and limited stakeholder coordination, threatening key species such as groupers, snappers, and parrotfish, as well as sensitive coral reef ecosystems. The development of a Reef Fishes Management Plan (RFMP) is critical to ensuring sustainable resource use, establishing enforceable governance mechanisms, and promoting inclusive development that balances ecological integrity with economic and social benefits.

Scope of Activity

1.Scope Of Work

The consultant shall undertake a comprehensive and participatory process to develop a Reef Fishes Management Plan that ensures ecological sustainability, socio-economic equity, and institutional effectiveness. The scope of work includes:
1.1.Literature Review and Baseline Assessment
·Review existing data, reports, and scientific literature on reef fish species, habitats, and fisheries in Tanzania’s Indian Ocean.
·Assess ecological status, fishing pressure, gear types, and socio-economic dynamics of reef fisheries.
·Identify critical data gaps and propose strategies for future research and monitoring.

1.2.Stakeholder Mapping and Engagement
·Identify and map key stakeholders, including artisanal fishers, women and youth groups, local government authorities, NGOs, and private sector actors.
·Conduct inclusive consultations and focus group discussions to gather local knowledge, perceptions, and priorities.
·Ensure gender-sensitive and culturally appropriate engagement strategies.

1.3.Policy and Legal Framework Analysis
·Review national policies (e.g., Fisheries Act, Blue Economy Strategy), regional protocols (e.g., SWIOFC), and international instruments (e.g., FAO Code of Conduct).
·Analyze institutional mandates, regulatory gaps, and enforcement mechanisms relevant to reef fisheries.
·Ensure the management plan is legally compliant and policy compliant.

1.4.Development of Management Measures
·Propose science-based and community-informed management measures such as:
oGear restrictions
oSeasonal closures
oCatch limits
oSpecies-specific protections

oMarine Protected Areas (MPAs) and no-take zones
·Integrate ecosystem-based and climate-resilient approaches.

1.5.Spatial Planning and Zoning
·Recommend spatial zoning strategies within the MPAs to balance conservation, fishing access, and livelihood needs.
·Align zoning proposals with existing Marine Spatial Planning initiatives and MPAs.

1.6.Capacity Building and Institutional Strengthening
·Assess institutional and community capacity gaps.
·Propose training modules, knowledge-sharing platforms, and institutional support mechanisms.
·Recommend partnerships for technical and financial sustainability.

1.7.Drafting and Validation of the Management Plan
·Prepare a Draft Reef Fishery Management Plan for the MPAs incorporating all technical, ecological, and stakeholder inputs.
·Facilitate validation workshops with stakeholders and government agencies.
Finalize the plan based on feedback and submit for official endorsement.

procnotices.notice_text:
Request for Expressions of Interest (REoI)

CONSULTING SERVICE:

Financial Management Specialist

PROJECT NAME:

Health Sector Transformation Project

PROJECT ID:

P181385

ACTIVITY REFERENCE:

SS-MOH-546379-CS-INDV

PROCUREMENT METHOD

Individual Consultant Selection

DUTY STATION/COUNTRY:

Ministry of Health, Juba, South Sudan

 

Background: The Ministry of Health (MoH) has received funding from the World Bank towards the cost of recruitment of a Financial Management Specialist to Support the fiduciary functions in the Project Management Unit (PMU) established under the MOH.  The project is to (i) provides a package of basic health and nutrition services based on the principle of continuum of care throughout the lifecycle (childhood, adolescence/adulthood, pregnancy, childbirth, postnatal period), and among the models of service delivery (including clinical care settings, outreach, and household and communities); and (ii) supports the primary care facilities nationwide with the basic inputs for maintaining their operational capacity.

Objective: The consulting services (“the Services”) is for Financial Management Specialist who will work within the Ministry’s Project Management Unit (PMU) and the main objective of this position is to support the Ministry of Health to build sound financial management systems and structures.  The Specialist expected to consider all the elements of the Public Financial Management PFM cycle such as budget preparation, budget execution, budget monitoring, accounting and treasury management, internal control including internal audit, financial reporting and external audits. As part of strengthening the accounts and finance function, the Specialist expected to be a central resource in supporting the MoH by establishing an effective and efficient financial management system MoH.

Key Responsibilities: These include but are not limited to the following:

  • Provide financial management support to the Project Management Unit. The Financial Management Specialist will be responsible for the all the financial management matters for the project.
  • Prepare Annual Work Plan and Budgets (AWPB), accompanying forecasts and financial analysis.
  • Review and verify payment vouchers and journal entries to ensure accuracy in financial data, reconciliations, and compliance with the Financing Agreement, World Bank (WB) rules and procedures, Government of South Sudan Laws and Regulations, Project Operations Manual, and the Finance Manual.

Terms of Reference: The detailed Terms of Reference (ToRs) containing roles and scope for the assignment can be obtained upon written request to the e-mail address: hstproject123@gmail.com  clearly indicating the subject matter as “ToR for Financial Management Specialist”.

Qualifications Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, business administration or related field, (ii) An advanced (Masters) degree in accounting, finance, economics, business or any related fields from a recognized university; (ii) Relevant professional qualification such as ACCA, CIPFA, CPA or equivalent, and membership of a recognized professional body in good and regular standing will be added advantage; (iii) At least, Seven (7) years of post-qualification experience handling financial management responsibilities in the public sector and/or projects financed by development partners,

Experience: (i) At least minimum seven years of experience should be related to financial management responsibilities in projects funded by the World Bank or similar international organizations; (ii) Good knowledge and application of relevant computerized accounting software such as QuickBooks / Navision or Pastel; (iii) Experience of Project Financial Management with international aid and development sector in FCV countries in sub-Sahara African and particularly South Sudan is highly desirable; (iv)Excellent written and oral communication skills, in English, to deliver complex technical documents, and reports; and (viii) Excellent computer skills, including Excel is required.

The shortlisted candidates will be invited for oral interview. Consultant will be required to possess the skills, concepts, knowledge and principles listed in the TOR.

Government officials or civil servants will not be considered unless: (i) they are on leave of absence without pay or have resigned or retired six months prior to the date of the advert; and (ii) their employment will not create Conflict of interest.

Selection Criteria: The Consultant(s) will be selected in accordance with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, dated July 2016 and revised 7th Edition of September 2025 which can be found at the following website: www.worldbank.org/procurement. Individual Consultant Selection (ICS) method will be used, and the first step shall be shortlisting based on the above qualification and experience requirements. This will then be followed by oral interviews for the shortlisted candidates and to be assessed using scored criteria as: (i) Qualification – 20%, (ii) Specific experience – 50%, and (iii) Desirable skills – 30%. 

Duration of the Assignment: The initial duration of the consultancy services is Twelve (12) months and shall be subject to renewal annually based on the performance and availability of funds.

Avis d’Appel d’offres

Pays : République Démocratique du Congo

Nom du Projet : Health Emergency Preparedness, Response, and Resilience Project

                                 « HEPRR-MPA »

 

Numéro du Crédit/Don : P504532

 

Intitulé du Marché : PRODUCTION ET DEPLOIEMENT D’OUTILS DE COMMUNICATION ET DE SENSIBILISATION CREC ADAPTES AUX CONTEXTES DE ROUTINE ET D’URGENCE, DESTINES AUX PROVINCES DE L’ÉQUATEUR, KASAÏ CENTRAL, KASAÏ, KASAÏ ORIENTAL, MAI-NDOMBE, TSHOPO, ITURI ET NORD-KIVU, EN DEUX (2) LOTS DISTINCTS. 

 

Référence : DAON N° ZR-DRC-MSP-536624-NC-RFB

 

1. Le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo (RDC) a reçu un financement de la Banque Mondiale pour financer le Projet de préparation, de réponse et de la résilience aux urgences sanitaires de la République Démocratique du Congo (RDC) en utilisant l’approche programmatique en plusieurs phases « HEPPR-MPA » et à l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché de production et déploiement d’outils de communication et de sensibilisation CREC adaptes aux contextes de routine et d’urgence, destines aux provinces de L’ÉQUATEUR, KASAÏ CENTRAL, KASAÏ, KASAÏ ORIENTAL, MAI-NDOMBE, TSHOPO, ITURI ET NORD-KIVU, en deux (2) lots distincts, à savoir :

                 

  • LOT 1 : Production, impression et déploiement des supports imprimés de communication et de sensibilisation CREC ;
  • LOT 2 : Production, déploiement et pose des supports rigides, de signalétique et des autres outils durables de communication et de sensibilisation CREC. 

 

2. Le Ministère de la Santé Publique à travers l’Unité de Gestion du Programme de Développement du Système de Santé sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour la production et déploiement desdits d’outils de communication et de sensibilisation CREC adaptes aux contextes de routine et d’urgence.

 

3. La passation du Marché sera conduite par Mise en Concurrence nationale en recourant à un Appel d’offres (AO)  telle que définie dans le Règlement de la Banque mondiale applicable aux Emprunteurs – Passation des Marchés dans le cadre de Financement de Projets d’Investissement daté de Juillet 2016, révisé en novembre 2017, Aout 2018, Novembre 2020, juillet 2023 , février 2025 et septembre 2025 ; et ouverte à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans le Règlement de passation des marchés.

 

4. Les Soumissionnaires intéressés et éligibles peuvent obtenir des informations auprès de l’Unité de Gestion du Programme de Développement du Système de Santé
(UG-PDSS) – Dr Dominique BAABO KUBUYA, courriel : heprr-mpa.msphps@ugpdss.org  avec copie à claudeogou@ugpdss.org; omboilenga@ugpdss.org et ciruziadolphe@ugpdss.org  et prendre connaissance du Dossier d’Appel d’offres à l’adresse mentionnée Nº1 ci-dessous de 9h00 à 15h30 heure locale (GMT+1) :

 

5. Le dossier d’Appel d’offres complet en Français peut être acheté par tout Soumissionnaire intéressé en formulant une demande écrite à l’adresse ci-dessous contre un paiement non remboursable de Cent dollars Américain (100 $US). La méthode de paiement sera par dépôt ou par virement sur le compte ci-dessous indiqué contre un récépissé de paiement.

Nom de la Banque : ECOBANK RDC

Le dossier d’appel d’offres sera adressé par voie électronique.

 

6. Les offres devront être remises à l’adresse ci-dessous au plus tard le 08 juin 2026 à 11h00 heure locale (GMT+1). La soumission des offres par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. Les offres remises en retard ne seront pas acceptées. Les offres seront ouvertes en présence des représentants des soumissionnaires et des personnes présentes à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous le 08 juin 2026 à 11h30 heure locale.

 

7. Toutes les offres doivent comprendre une Garantie bancaire de l’offre d’un montant indiqué ci-dessous, ou l’équivalent dans une monnaie librement convertible :

  • Lot 1 : 7 500 $US (Dollars américains quatre mille).

L’attention est attirée sur le Règlement de Passation de Marchés exigeant que l’Emprunteur divulgue des informations sur la propriété effective du Soumissionnaire retenu, dans le cadre de la Notification d’Attribution du Marché, en utilisant le Formulaire de Divulgation des Bénéficiaires Effectifs tel qu’il est inclus dans le document d’appel d’offres.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include Consultancy Services to Develop the Strategic Marketing Plan and Value Chain Analysis For Octopus, Prawns, Mud Crab, and Lobster Fisheries In Tanzania.
3.The MINISTRY OF LIVESTOCK AND FISHERIES - TASFAM now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested

Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services for a period of 150.

Number of Required Key Personnel    3

Description of Services


Tanzania’s marine fisheries sector plays a vital role in food security, livelihoods, and export earnings. Species such as octopus, prawns, mud crab, and lobster are high-value commodities with growing demand in regional and international markets. However, these fisheries face challenges including fragmented value chains, limited market intelligence, poor infrastructure, and weak branding. Under the TASFAM Project, the Government of Tanzania seeks to strengthen the competitiveness and sustainability of these fisheries by conducting a comprehensive value chain analysis and developing strategic marketing plans that promote inclusive growth, climate resilience, and responsible trade. The consultancy will inform policy, investment, and capacity-building efforts to enhance competitiveness, sustainability, and inclusivity in processing and trade.

Scope of Activity

The assignment will be carried out in the coastal districts of Tanzania Mainland, focusing on specified tasks. The consultant will perform several tasks, including, but they are not limited to: -

A.Value Chain Mapping

·Identify key actors, functions, and relationships across the supply chain Analyze margins, volumes, and governance structures
·Map infrastructure, logistics, and service provision gaps. Identify all actors from harvest to end-market (fishers, middlemen, processors, exporters)
·Assess Harvesting and Post-Harvest Practices
·Evaluate Infrastructure and Support Services
·Examine Governance and Regulatory Frameworks
·Assess Social Inclusion and Equity, examine gender roles, youth participation, and community engagement, and propose strategies for inclusive value chain upgrading
·.Identify Opportunities for Value Addition and Innovation
Explore potential for product diversification (e.g., frozen tails, crab meat, ready-to-cook packs)

B.Market Analysis

·Conduct market research on domestic and export opportunities
·Assess buyer preferences, quality standards, and certification schemes
·Identify trade barriers and investment opportunities
·Assess the current market dynamics, supply chains, and value addition for octopus, lobsters, and prawns.
·Assess domestic, regional, and international demand trends
·Identify key consumer segments, preferences, and purchasing behaviors.
·Assess current market channels, pricing structures, and consumer preferences.
·Map existing market channels (local markets, hotels, export routes) and their performance.

·Analyze pricing structures, margins, and competitiveness across the value chain.
·Evaluate environmental and social impacts of marketing strategies, including sustainability of the resources and inclusivity

C.Stakeholder Engagement

·Facilitate consultations with fishers, processors, traders, exporters, regulators, and community groups.
·Document stakeholder priorities and validate proposed interventions
·Integrate gender and youth perspectives

D.Strategic Marketing Plan Development

·Develop species-specific marketing strategies, including:
oBranding and product differentiation
oQuality assurance and traceability systems
oPromotion and market entry strategies
oIdentify gaps in policy, regulation, and institutional coordination affecting marketing.
oRecommend policy reforms or incentives to support seafood marketing and investment.

E.Policy and Institutional Recommendations

·Propose reforms to improve governance, licensing, and investment climate
·Recommend infrastructure upgrades and capacity-building needs
·Align marketing strategies with national blue economy goals and fisheries governance frameworks

procnotices.notice_text:
FAS – INSTITUTO DE DESENVOLVIMENTO LOCAL

                 PROJECTO DE REFORÇO DO SISTEMA DE PROTECÇÃO SOCIAL                           PARA O CAPITAL HUMANO E A RESILIÊNCIA – KWENDA II

 

                                             Solicitação de Propostas (Bens)

País:

Angola

Nome do Projecto:

Projecto de Reforço do Sistema de Protecção Social para o Capital Humano e a Resiliência – KWENDA II

Título do contrato:

Aquisição de Equipamentos de Protecção Individual no âmbito da Inclusão Produtiva

Empréstimo N.º

BIRD - 9718-AO

Referência da SDP:

AO-MAT FAS-530696-GO-RFB

Emitido em:

14 de Maio de 2026
  1. O Governo de Angola recebeu crédito do Banco Mundial para custear o Projecto de Reforço do Sistema de Protecção Social para o Capital Humano e a Resiliência – KWENDA II, e pretende aplicar parte dos fundos para pagamento de contrato para Aquisição de Equipamentos de Protecção Individual no âmbito da Inclusão Produtiva. Os pagamentos relativos a este contrato serão efectuados pelo Mutuário em conformidade com os termos e condições estabelecidos no contrato, em observância às regras e procedimentos do Banco Mundial aplicáveis à gestão de fundos do Projecto.
  2. O FAS – Instituto de Desenvolvimento Local convida os Concorrentes elegíveis a apresentarem propostas seladas para Aquisição de Equipamentos de Protecção Individual no âmbito da Inclusão Produtiva, esta aquisição refere-se á:

Lote 1- Botas

 Galochas e Botas de Segurança

Lote 2- Material de Uniformes

Fato Macacão Personalizados, Capas de Chuvas, Aventais personalizados, Luvas de Serralharia, Luvas de Construção Civil

Lote 3- Material de Protecção

Capacetes  de Segurança; Óculos de Proteção para Soldadura; Luvas de Serralharia;  Chapéus para Agricultores; Toucas personalizadas

3. O processo será conduzido através de concurso nacional usando uma Solicitação de Propostas (RFB), conforme especificado no documento do Banco Mundial “Regulamentos de Aquisição para Mutuários do IPF” datado de julho de 2016, tendo a sua última actualização em setembro de 2025, e está aberta aos licitantes qualificados, conforme definido nos Regulamentos de Aquisição.

4. Os Concorrentes elegíveis interessados podem obter mais informações no endereço abaixo. Também deverão ser levantados os cadernos de encargos pelos Concorrentes interessados mediante um pedido ou registo por escrito. O documento poderá ser obtido no endereço abaixo indicado ou, mediante solicitação, enviado por correio eletrónico.

5. As propostas deverão ser entregues na Direcção Geral do FAS até às 10h00 do dia 25 de Junho de 2026. Apresentação das propostas electrónicas não serão permitidas. As propostas atrasadas serão rejeitadas, as propostas serão abertas na presença dos representantes dos concorrentes que desejarem assistir pessoalmente no endereço abaixo de acordo com o período estipulados no caderno de encargos.

6. Todas as Propostas devem ser acompanhadas por uma Declaração de Garantia da Proposta.

7. Chama-se a atenção para o Regulamento de Aquisições que exige que o Mutuário divulgue informações sobre a propriedade beneficiária do licitante vencedor, como parte do Aviso de Adjudicação do Contrato, usando o Formulário de Divulgação de Propriedade Beneficiária conforme incluído no documento de licitação.

8. O endereço acima referido é:

procnotices.project_name: Log-In Georgia
procnotices.bid_description: Engineer Consultancy Services for Civil Works of Fiber Optic Infrastructure Rollout (Khulo-Akhaltsikhe-Borjomi)
procnotices.contact_address: Nikoloz Kipshidze Str. N7b, Tbilisi 0162, Georgia
procnotices.notice_text:
The Government of Georgia signed a Loan Agreement with the World Bank for the Log-In Georgia Project. The project aims to increase access to affordable broadband internet and to promote its use by individuals and enterprises in targeted rural settlements.  Open Net N(N)L is the Project Implementing Unit (PIU).  

Within the framework of the Log-In Georgia Project, the PIU is announcing a Request for  Expression of Interest (REOI) for the “Engineer Consultancy Services”.  

The objectives of this consultant assignment are to supervise civil works for the construction of fiber optic infrastructure in the Khulo-Akhaltsikhe-Borjomi region (the details are available at the links in the Georgian Electronic-Government Procurement System (Ge-GP): https://tenders.procurement.gov.ge/public/?go=631277&lang=ge ) to ensure that the works are executed within the contractual time and budget and comply with the approved design, specifications, environmental and social requirements, and sound engineering practices.  Detailed information on the assignment can be obtained from the TOR, which is available at the following link: https://opennet.ge/en/read/5346

Interested firms are expected to express their interest by providing general but comprehensive information indicating that they could be qualified to perform the service (according to the TOR requirements). At the stage of EOI, you are not requested and, therefore, must not present a financial proposal. A consulting firm will be selected in accordance with the procedures set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrower dated July 2016 (the seventh Edition, September 2025).  Expressions of Interest must be delivered electronically to the mailing address procurement@opennet.ge.

TONGA SAFE RESILIENT SCHOOL PROJECT (TSRSP)

Assignment Title: Recruitment of Development of a Strategic School Infrastructure Development Pla

Reference No: TO-MET-394589-CS-INDV

The Ministry of Education and Training has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Tonga Safe and Resilient Schools Project (TSRSP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment an be found by Ctrl + Click to follow

29042026 TOR_Infrastructure Development and Management Plan_Final - Google Docs

OR

can be obtained at the address given below.

Firms’ staff may express interest through the employing firm for the assignment and, under such situation, only the experience and qualifications of individuals shall be considered in the selection process.

The Ministry of Education and Training via the TSRSP now invites eligible individual (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services by submitting:

  1. Cover letter stating your interest and responding to the selection criteria (maximum 2 pages)
  2. Resume and Supporting Documents to demonstrate that you meet the minimum requirements (maximum 5 pages).

The criteria for selecting the Consultants are provided in detail in the TOR but not limited to:

  1. At least an advanced degree in facilities management, facilities maintenance, strategic planning, management, public policy, development studies, business, or other relevant discipline from a recognized university.
  2. Relevant work experience in facilities management maintenance, infrastructure planning and/or development
  3. Must have experience working with government agencies especially education and its stakeholders.
  4. Knowledge and understanding of infrastructure or asset management practices and challenges in the Pacific.
  5. Knowledge in the general social, economic and political environment that influences education infrastructure landscape in Tonga and the Pacific.
  6. Professional oral and written communication skills in English, including via email, audio/videoconference and face to face with government officials.
  7. Proven analytical skills and ability to conceptualise and write concisely and clearly.
  8. Ability to work independently, deliver under pressure/meet timelines, and resolve technical issues.
  9. Knowledge of relevant Tongan Legislations for infrastructure, asset management and Tonga strategic goals will be an advantage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants (including firms) is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.
